source_text: De exitu plane, puto, diuersitatem temptatis inducere, negantes passionem crucis in Christum creatoris praedicatam et argumentantes insuper non esse credendum, ut in id genus mortis exposuerit creator filium suum, quod ipse maledixerat: maledictus, inquit, omnis qui pependerit in ligno. sed huius maledictionis sensum differo digne a sola praedicatione crucis, de qua nunc maxime quaeritur, quia et alias antecedit rerum probatio rationem. de figuris prius edocebo. et utique uel maxime sacramentum istud figurari in praedicatione oportebat, quanto incredibile, tanto magis scandalo futurum. si nude praedicaretur, quantoque magnificum, tanto magis obumbrandum, ut difficultas intellectus gratiam dei quaereret. itaque inprimis Isaac, cum a patre in hostiam deditus lignum sibi portaret ipse, Christi exitum iam tunc denotabat, in uictimam concessi a patre et lignum passionis suae baiulantis. Ioseph. et ipse Christum figuraturus, uel hoc solo, ne demorer cursum. quod persecutionem a fratribus passus est ob dei gratiam. sicut et Christus a Iudaeis carnaliter (fratribus,) cum benedicitur a patre etiam in haec uerba: tauri decor eius, cornua unicornis cornua eius, in eis nationes uentilabit pariter ad summum usque terrae, non utique rhinoceros destinabatur unicornis nec minotaurus bicornis, sed Christus in illo significabatur, taurus ob utramque dispositionem, aliis ferus ut iudex, aliis mansuetus ut saluator, cuius cornua essent crucis extima. nam et in antemna, quae crucis pars est, extremitates cornua uocantur, unicornis autem mediae stipitis palus. hac denique uirtute crucis et hoc more cornutus uniuersas gentes et nunc uentilat per fidem, auferens a terra in caelum, et tunc per iudicium uentilabit, deiciens de caelo in terram. idem erit et alibi taurus apud eandem scripturam, cum Iacob in Simeonem et Leui, id est in scribas et Pharisaeos, — ex illis enim deducitur census. istorum — spiritaliter imprecatur: Simeon et Leui perfecerunt iniquitatem ex sua haeresi, qua scilicet Christum sunt persecuti; in consilium eorum ne uenerit anima mea et in stationem eorum ne incubuerint iecora mea, quia in indignatione sua interfecerunt homines, id est prophetas, et in concupiscentia sua ceciderunt neruos tauro, id est Christo, quem post necem prophetarum suffigendo neruos utique eius clauis desaeuierunt. ceterum uanum, si post homicidia alicuius bouis illis exprobrat carnificinam. iam uero Moyses, quid utique tunc tantum, cum Iesus aduersus Amalech proeliabatur, expansis manibus orat residens, quando in rebus tam attonitis magis utique genibus depositis et manibus caedentibus pectus et facie humi uolutante orationem commendare debuisset, nisi quia illic, ubi nomen domini dimicabat, dimicaturi quandoque aduersus diabolum, crucis quoque erat habitus necessarius, per quam Iesus uictoriam esset relaturus? idem rursus Moyses post interdictam omnis rei similitudinem cur aereum serpentem ligno impositum pendentis habitu in spectaculum salutare proposuit? an et hic dominicae crucis uim intentabat, qua serpens diabolus publicabatur et laeso cuique a spiritalibus colubris, intuenti tamen et credenti in eam, sanitas morsuum peccatorum et salus exinde praedicabatur?
pass_a_gloss: Marcion denies cross for Creator’s Christ; Tertullian: cross sacrament veiled in figures — Isaac’s wood, Joseph’s persecution, bull-horns as cross ends, Moses’ spread arms and bronze serpent — so looking/believing yields healing and salvation.
pass_b_english: On the outcome itself, I think, you try to force a difference, denying that the passion of the cross was preached for the Creator’s Christ, and arguing besides that it is not to be believed the Creator exposed his Son to that kind of death which he himself had cursed: Cursed, he says, is everyone who hangs on a tree. But I put off the sense of this curse, worthily, from the mere preaching of the cross — which is now the chief question — because elsewhere the proof of the facts also goes before the reason. I will teach first from the figures. And of course this sacrament especially had to be figured in preaching — the more incredible, the more it would be a scandal if preached bare, and the more magnificent, the more it had to be veiled, so that the difficulty of understanding would seek the grace of God. And so first Isaac, when handed over by the father as a victim and himself carrying the wood, was already then marking Christ’s exit — yielded by the Father as victim and bearing the wood of his own passion. Joseph too was going to figure Christ — if only by this, so I do not delay the run: that he suffered persecution from his brothers because of God’s grace, as Christ also from the Jews, brothers after the flesh — when he is blessed by the father even in these words: His beauty is a bull’s, his horns the horns of a unicorn; with them he will fan the nations alike to the end of the earth. Not that a rhinoceros was being destined as unicorn, nor a two-horned minotaur, but Christ was being signified in him — a bull for either arrangement: to some fierce as judge, to some gentle as savior — whose horns would be the ends of the cross. For even on the yardarm, which is part of the cross, the extremities are called horns, and the unicorn is the stake of the middle post. By this power of the cross, then, and horned in this way, he even now fans all the nations through faith, lifting them from earth to heaven, and then through judgment he will fan them, casting them from heaven to earth. The same will also be the bull elsewhere in the same scripture, when Jacob spiritually curses Simeon and Levi — that is, the scribes and Pharisees (for from them their census is drawn): Simeon and Levi finished iniquity from their heresy, by which of course they persecuted Christ; into their counsel let my soul not come, and on their station let my liver not lie, because in their indignation they killed men — that is, the prophets — and in their desire they cut the bull’s sinews — that is, Christ’s — whom after the prophets’ murder they raged against by nailing his sinews with nails. Otherwise it is empty if after someone’s cattle-slaughter he rebukes them for butchery. But now Moses — why then only, when Joshua was fighting against Amalek, does he pray with hands spread while sitting, when in affairs so startling he ought rather to have recommended prayer with knees set down and hands beating the breast and face rolling on the ground — unless because there, where the Lord’s name was fighting, about to fight someday against the devil, the habit of the cross was also necessary, through which Jesus would bring back victory? Again the same Moses, after every likeness of a thing was forbidden — why did he set out a bronze serpent placed on wood in the habit of one hanging, as a saving spectacle? Or was he here too aiming the force of the Lord’s cross, by which the serpent-devil was published, and for anyone hurt by spiritual snakes, yet looking and believing on it, healing of the bites of sins and salvation from then on was preached?

lemmas.lat: passionem crucis in Christum creatoris praedicatam
lemmas.sense: the passion of the cross preached for the Creator’s Christ
cursed is everyone who hangs on a tree
bearing the wood of his own passion
whose horns would be the ends of the cross

choices.why: passio crucis is the concrete cross-death at issue vs Marcion.
lignum passionis ties Isaac’s wood to the cross as type.
crucis extima is Tertullian’s explicit cross-geometry gloss.

notes: Cross/prophecy locus beyond prior 4.40 Pascha tip; Creator’s Christ crucified.
